title: Personal OKRs & Weekly Check-in - Feb 28 2026
content:
Notes (brain dump) - Feb 24-28, 2026

Context / quick snapshot:
- Q1 OKRs: focus on RU-serve throughput, p95 latency, and on-call readiness for Dedicated customers.
- Personal stretch: ship model-fallback policy and a first-pass experiment on KV-cache heuristics.

Top-level KPIs (quantifiable) - current status:
- p95 token latency (hosted API): goal <= 120ms, current 138ms (up from 152ms last week)
- throughput (tokens/sec per GPU): goal +15% vs baseline, current +9% (need another +6%)
- Dedicated customer SLOs: 99.9% uptime for reserved pools - last week 99.94% (good)
- PRs merged affecting inference kernel selection: 2/3 (fallback PR still in review)

This week highlights / accomplishments:
- Fixed a regression in batching logic that caused starvation for short requests - measurable p50 improvement for chat workloads.
- Mentored Sam on the KV cache profiling harness; he added latency histograms for cold-starts (nice).
- Quick spike on allocator tuning: saw 8% throughput bump in microbenchmarks (needs integration test).

Open blockers / risks:
- Fallback policy PR (github:pull/2384) has unresolved UX questions for rollback behavior. Need design sync with Product (Maya) - schedule for Monday.
- Autoscaler flapping seen in a specific Dedicated cluster under mixed workloads - suspected config mismatch (investigate policy thresholds).
- Regression tests are slow; CI queue causing delays for critical merges (talk to release-eng about parallelization).

Personal OKR draft (for Q1 -> Q2 handoff) - proposed:
O: Deliver reliable inference improvements that reduce customer token-costs and improve latency.
KR1: Reduce hosted API p95 latency from 150ms -> <=120ms across 3 representative models (measurement: perf-bench v2).
KR2: Increase tokens/sec per-GPU by 15% on average across production workloads via batching/kernel-selection changes.
KR3: Ship model-fallback and canary rollout flow with automatic rollback integration (docs + console support).

Actions for next week (concrete):
- Monday: 30m sync with Maya to finalize fallback UX and rollback signals. (owner: Ryan)
- Tuesday: Pair with Sam to wire KV cold-start histograms into perf dashboard and add alert for cold-start > 200ms.
- Wed-Thu: Finish integration tests for allocator changes, get perf-run tagged in CI. (goal: get at least one green perf-run)
- Friday: Cut a canary for fallback policy in staging, run 200k chat tokens through staged path, gather regressions.
- Ongoing: triage autoscaler logs for Dedicated cluster alpha-3, escalate to infra if root cause identified.

Personal development goals (non-OKR):
- Continue mentoring: schedule bi-weekly 1:1 learning sessions with Sam and Priya (short 30m deep dives).
- Docs: write a short howto (1-2 pages) on "model fallback best practices" for console team. Target publish by Mar 14.

Retro notes / learnings from last sprint:
- Small, frequent experiments (allocator knobs + batching policy) are higher ROI than big rewrites. Keep iterations small.
- When a perf regression ships, the quickest path is a scoped rollback + narrow fix; invest more in quick rollback automation.
- Improving signal (better perf tests and more representative workloads) reduced time-to-detect from ~3 days -> ~12 hours in Feb. Keep extending coverage.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Decide metric for rollback safety (is perf delta + error-rate combined threshold enough?). -> Discuss with SRE and Product next week.
- How to quantify customer-visible cost-savings from quantization recommendations? Need an experiment plan.

Quick list (scratch):
- PRs to follow up: #2384 (fallback), #2410 (allocator), #2398 (batching fixes).
- Customers to ping re: Dedicated autoscaler behavior: AcmeHealth, FinData (get logs/trace ids).
- Reminders: submit Q1 retrospective notes to eng-retros docs by Mar 1.

Final thought: prioritize shipping a small, well-tested fallback path rather than perfecting heuristics. Customers value robustness and predictable behavior.

End of note.
